title: Isolation and Imaging of Microvessels From Brain Tissue
author: Josephine K. Buff
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: The day before the experiment, coat slides with 300 µL poly‑D‑lysine (PDL) each, cover and incubate at room temperature (RT) overnight; wash off excess PDL with ddH₂O and let dry at RT. Prepare 1 % BSA in PBS and 32 % dextran solution according to the recipes. Cool a 500 mL bottle of PBS at 4 °C overnight. Label one 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, one 15 mL conical tube, one 50 mL conical tube and one 40 µm cell strainer per sample. Prepare 1 % BSA + 1× protease inhibitor (PI) in PBS, keep on ice. Fill each labeled 15 mL tube with 10 mL 32 % dextran solution and keep on ice. Place Dounce homogenizers on ice and cut 5 mm off the ends of 1 000 µL pipette tips (one modified tip per sample).

steps.title: Chop brain tissue
steps.instruction: Place a mouse brain hemisphere (≈0.2 mg) in a 60 mm Petri dish on ice, add 0.5 mL 1 % BSA + 1× PI in PBS, and cut the tissue into ~1 mm³ pieces with a razor blade; pieces should pass through the precut 1 000 µL tip but not through an uncut tip.

steps.title: Transfer and wash tissue
steps.instruction: Using the precut 1 000 µL tip, transfer the chopped tissue to the Dounce homogenizer tube on ice. Wash the razor blade and Petri dish with an additional 1 mL 1 % BSA + 1× PI in PBS and transfer as much tissue as possible to the Dounce tube with the same precut tip.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Insert the pestle, gently push it to the bottom, then move it up and down to disperse tissue along the tube walls. Perform ~20 gentle up‑and‑down strokes without pulling the pestle out, keeping the homogenizer submerged in ice and avoiding bubbles, twisting, or excessive compression.

steps.title: Combine with dextran solution
steps.instruction: Using a 5 mL serological pipette, transfer the homogenate to the labeled 15 mL conical tube containing 10 mL 32 % dextran. Wash the Dounce tube and pestle with 1 mL 1 % BSA + 1× PI in PBS using a 1 000 µL pipette and add the wash to the same 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Mix and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Invert the 15 mL tube roughly 20 times to fully homogenize the mixture. Centrifuge at 4 400 × g for 25 min at 4 °C with slow deceleration.

steps.title: Remove unwanted layers
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, carefully aspirate the top myelin layer with a 5 mL serological pipette (clean tube interior with a Kimwipe if needed). Then aspirate the middle parenchymal layer with a 10 mL serological pipette, leaving ~1 mL supernatant above the vascular pellet; avoid disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Prepare strainer for collection
steps.instruction: Place a labeled 40 µm cell strainer on a 50 mL conical tube. Wet the strainer by adding 5 mL 1 % BSA in PBS, ensuring all mesh areas are wetted.

steps.title: Resuspend vascular pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the vascular pellet in the 15 mL tube with 1 mL 1 % BSA + 1× PI in PBS, then add the suspension to the wetted 40 µm strainer.

steps.title: Wash microvessels
steps.instruction: Wash the strainer with 30 mL cold PBS using a 25 mL serological pipette, adding the PBS slowly to avoid overflow or dissociation of microvessels.

steps.title: Fix microvessels (optional)
steps.instruction: Place the strainer in a 150 mm Petri dish containing 4 % PFA solution, cover with aluminum foil, and place on a gentle shaker for 15 min at RT. Ensure no air is trapped beneath the strainer. (Omit this step for downstream applications that require live tissue.)

steps.title: Post‑fix washes
steps.instruction: Transfer the strainer to an empty 50 mL conical tube and wash with 20 mL cold PBS.

steps.title: Collect microvessels from strainer
steps.instruction: Invert the strainer over a labeled 50 mL conical tube and wash it with 20 mL 1 % BSA in PBS, adding the liquid slowly so it passes through the mesh; ensure all sides are washed and collect the flow‑through.

steps.title: Pellet microvessels
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 2 000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C with slow deceleration.

steps.title: Resuspend and store pellet
steps.instruction: Remove as much supernatant as possible without disturbing the pellet. Use the remaining 100–400 µL supernatant to resuspend the microvessel pellet and transfer the suspension to a labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. Store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks (pause point).

steps.title: Prepare slides for staining
steps.instruction: Draw up to six rectangles per PDL‑coated slide with a hydrophobic barrier pen, place slides in a 150 mm Petri dish and let the barriers dry before proceeding.

steps.title: Plate microvessels on slides
steps.instruction: Gently resuspend microvessels in the microcentrifuge tube by pipetting up and down with a 1 000 µL tip. Add ~30 µL of suspension to each rectangle, then loosely cover the dish with aluminum foil and let the slides dry overnight at RT.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL blocking solution to each rectangle, loosely cover with foil, and incubate 1 h at RT. (Amount may vary with rectangle size.)

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Remove blocking solution. Add primary antibodies diluted 1:250 in 30 µL blocking solution per rectangle (AQP4 and CD31) and incubate 1 h at RT, loosely covered with foil.

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash three times with 30 µL TBS‑T for 5 min each (TBS‑T may be replaced by TBS or PBS if permeabilization is not needed).

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add secondary antibodies diluted 1:500 in 30 µL blocking solution per rectangle (donkey anti‑goat Alexa 488 and donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa 555) and incubate 1 h at RT, loosely covered with foil; protect slides from light from this step onward.

steps.title: Wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash twice with 30 µL TBS‑T and once with PBS, each for 5 min.

steps.title: Mount slides
steps.instruction: Remove the final PBS wash and let the microvessels dry. Add 20 µL mounting medium to each rectangle, place a coverslip avoiding air bubbles, and let the slides dry overnight at RT in a light‑protected ventilated area. Store slides at 4 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Image microvessels
steps.instruction: Using a confocal laser‑scanning microscope (e.g., Zeiss LSM880 with ZEN software), select a 40–63× oil‑immersion objective and appropriate lasers (647, 555, 488, 405 nm). Keep acquisition settings consistent across samples. Capture Z‑stacks centered on each region of interest with optimal slice thickness, acquiring several fields per sample for quantification.
